# Simulation-free real-to-real demonstration augmentation (sfagen): the method

**One pipeline, one configuration, several tasks.** Both OpenArm datasets are generated by exactly this code
([`sfagen`](README.md)) with identical robot, camera, reconstruction, planning, replay-check, rendering and evaluation
settings:
- `ethanCSL/openarm_pringles_lerobot_real_to_sim_10_3cam_v00` (bimanual hand-over);
- `ethanCSL/openarm_insertbattery_lerobot_real_to_sim_10_3cam_v00` (bimanual insertion).

Only the task description differs: source dataset, objects (with a proxy shape) and the variation grid.

Every output pixel is a real camera pixel; every trajectory is a kinematic edit of a recorded one. No simulator, no
generative model, no manual label.

```
 rig (once):   A camera calibration ── B table height
 per episode:  C reconstruction ── D variation planning ── E replay checks ── F rendering ── G wrist views
 dataset:      H export + verification          evaluation: I real-ground-truth benchmark, J coverage
```

## A. Camera calibration (once per rig)

- **Objective.** Render-and-compare: maximise the IoU between the z-buffered URDF silhouette and a camera-independent foreground, |frame − temporal median of all frames| > 30. Only near-static frames are used, so time offsets cannot bias the fit.
- **Parameters.** Rotation (3), translation (3) and log focal (1) relative to an initial guess; Powell's method; fit on even source episodes, evaluated on odd ones.
- **New rigs.** An optional coarse random search (±15°, ±15 cm) handles a rough initial guess.
- **Results.**
  - OpenArm battery rig: held-out IoU 0.248 → 0.299.
  - Pringles rig: held-out IoU 0.307 → 0.361.

## B. Table height (once per rig)

- **Known-size objects available.** For every source episode, fit the object's proxy (grasp-constrained, see C4) jointly with the table height to its frame-0 silhouette. If the median IoU ≥ 0.5, the table height is the median of the confident fits (Pringles: 0.200 m, IoU 0.58–0.84).
- **Otherwise.** The table height is the lowest arm point over the source demos − 5 mm (battery: the 18650 cell is too small to fit reliably, IoU ≈ 0.1–0.2).

## C. Reconstruction (per source episode)

1. **Robot geometry.** URDF visual meshes are area-sampled at 1.5 mm and z-buffered by a two-pass GPU point splat. Each geometry belongs to the arm whose joint is its nearest kinematic ancestor.
2. **Robot masks.** SAM2.1 (hiera-small) video segmentation.
   - **Prompts.** Every 15 frames each arm gets a mask prompt: the union of the projected convex hulls of its distal geometries, with object neighbourhoods removed.
   - **Processing.** The video is processed in independent 150-frame chunks, so GPU memory does not grow with episode length.
3. **Clean plate.** The temporal median over pixels free of the dilated robot and object silhouettes.
4. **Objects.** Each object is segmented as **what disappears when it is picked up**: frame 0 vs the median of robot-free pixels after the grasp.
   - **Known-size cylinders** (Pringles can, battery). The pose comes from render-and-compare constrained by the grasp kinematics.
     - The centre is the TCP at the grasp plus s·(approach axis) + l·(finger-closing axis), with s ∈ [−8, 8] cm and l ∈ [−4, 4] cm.
     - A lying cylinder's axis is perpendicular to the finger-closing axis.
     - The fit maximises silhouette IoU.
   - **Unknown size** (charging station). An oriented box from the segment (PCA extents, height from the grasp height).
   - **Holders.** Table → grasping hand (X = T_hand⁻¹ T_object) → hand-over to another closed hand / released.
5. **Video/state time offset.** Photometric: the offset in [−3, +0.5] frames (step 0.25) that best re-renders real frames from nearby real frames.
   - **Pairs.** 16 motion pairs (j, j+6), on a grid offset from the benchmark grid.
   - **Comparison.** Two silhouette-based scans were too flat to resolve offsets (≤ 0.004 IoU across offsets); the photometric score varies by 1.2–1.7 dB.

## D. Variations (kinematics; identical rules for every task)

| family | what moves | rule |
|---|---|---|
| **F1 object position** | an object resting on the table, by d (±3/±6 cm in x or y) | the grasping arm's TCP gets w(t)·d: smoothstep 0→1 from its motion onset to grasp − 15, 1 through grasp + 10, 1→0 until the **lift apex** (first height maximum within 4 s after the grasp, ≥ 30 frames after it, ≥ 10 frames before the next gripper event of any arm); recording afterwards ([MimicGen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17596), [DemoGen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16932)) |
| **F2 interaction location** (target position) | the whole multi-arm interaction (hand-over / insertion), by d (±3/±5 cm in x or y) | every arm's TCP gets w(t)·d over the window where the TCPs are < 20 cm apart, clipped to start after every grasp of a resting object + 10 frames and end before any put-down − 10 frames, 45-frame smoothstep ramps; hands and held objects move rigidly together, so all recorded contact relations are kept ([DexMimicGen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.24185)) |

**Shared by both families:**
- **Orientation:** unchanged.
- **IK:** bounded damped-least-squares IK (URDF limits ∪ recorded pose), warm-started along the source; joint offsets Gaussian-smoothed (σ = 3 frames).
- **Contact-exact refinement:** on frames where the full offset applies (object-relative approach and grasp; interaction window), the smoothed solution is refined by IK so the hand is exact where it touches; everything is re-verified by FK. This raised passing candidates from 41 to 96 (Pringles) and from 101 to 114 (battery); the failures had been 1–3 mm smoothing residuals.
- **Actions:** a′(t) = a(t) + Δq(t + k), with the recorded command-to-state lead k.
- **Grippers:** bit-identical to the recording.

## E. Replay checks (accept or reject; same thresholds for every task)

These are computed on the commanded action stream and the planned state:
- **Limits:** URDF joint limits ∪ the demo's own range.
- **Speed and acceleration:** speed ≤ 1.25× and acceleration ≤ 1.5× the maximum over all source demos.
- **Clearance:** coal arm–arm / arm–base mesh distance ≥ min(source over the same frames, 2 cm) − 1 mm.
- **Hands:** TCP distance ≥ source − 5 mm.
- **Table:** lowest arm point ≥ source minimum − 1 cm.
- **Start pose:** the recorded one.
- **Untouched parts:** non-moved arms and grippers bit-identical; frames after the rejoin identical.
- **IK:** ≤ 1 mm / 0.5° wherever the full offset applies (object-relative approach and grasp; interaction window), ≤ 5 mm / 2° while blending.
- **Objects:**
  - the lowest point never more than 5 mm below the source's;
  - a moved resting object stays in view and on the table (plate appearance like its original place);
  - it is ≥ 1 cm from other objects;
  - the robot is never closer to it before the final approach than the recorded robot was to the recorded object.

## F. Body-camera rendering: mesh-guided forward warping of real pixels

Per output frame:
1. **Background.** Pixels of moved parts are replaced by the clean plate relit to the frame (normalised-convolution log-ratio, σ = 10 px).
2. **Forward warp.**
   - Every real pixel of a moved part (robust mask: SAM2 ∪ plate-difference foreground within 12 px of the rendered part) gets a 3-D point from the mesh / proxy depth.
   - It is moved by its part's rigid motion, with z-tests.
   - Pinholes are closed by normalised convolution.
3. **Newly visible surfaces.** These are borrowed from other frames of the same recording (j ± 3k, k ≤ 15) where the same surface point is visible.
4. **Remaining holes.** Telea inpainting, then 3×3 median despeckle and 1-px anti-aliasing.
5. **Copied frames.** Frames whose scene equals the recording are copied.

**Fixed configuration:** `tm_erode` 21, `despeckle` on, `part_fill` off, `plate_adapt` 10.
- **Part-aware fill** was decided on development episodes of both tasks: Pringles −0.09 dB [−0.11, −0.07], battery +0.01 [−0.002, 0.016].

## G. Wrist cameras

These are real recorded wrist frames at the same time index. `wrist_view_valid = 1` where the whole scene equals the recording, and `wrist_view_pose_offset` gives the per-frame offset of each synthetic wrist.

## H. Export and verification

**Export.** LeRobot v3.0 (AV1). Two datasets per task:
- a synthetic-only dataset;
- a real + synthetic dataset: original real videos copied, plus a per-frame `is_synthetic` flag.

**Verification:**
- the dataset loads in LeRobot;
- state/action SHA-256 equals the plan;
- no episode equals a real episode;
- all frames decode, with no black frames;
- the body camera matches the renders (≈ 40 dB after encoding);
- every episode passes all replay checks.

## I. Real-ground-truth benchmark (renderer fidelity)

**Method.** Re-render real frame j+k from real frame j only (k = 4/8/15), with no texture borrowed within ±5 of the target. PSNR/SSIM are computed inside the foreground of both frames vs the temporal median, a region that depends on no pipeline. Episodes are held out from every tuning decision. CIs are episode-bootstrap 95%.

| task (held-out episodes, pairs) | copy source frame | published renderer | **unified sfagen** | unified − published |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Pringles (0,2,3,4,6,7,9; 211) | 14.51 dB | 17.87 dB | **18.05 dB** (SSIM 0.703 vs 0.692) | +0.17 dB [−0.06, 0.41], better in 55% |
| battery (3,5,8,9; 284) | 16.28 dB | 18.40 dB | **19.22 dB** (SSIM 0.709 vs 0.681) | +0.82 dB [0.64, 1.00], better in 74% |

**What made one pipeline at least as good as both task-specific ones.** On the Pringles held-out set:

| configuration | unified − published (dB) | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| 3-D-model masks only | −0.48 | −0.63 to −0.31 |
| + SAM2 masks | −0.30 | −0.46 to −0.13 |
| + photometric time offset, part fill off | **+0.17** | −0.06 to 0.41 |

## J. Coverage (what the synthetic data adds)

Object and target positions come from forward kinematics at gripper events. They are compared with the other real recordings of each task, which are never used for generation (see the dataset cards and `logs/coverage.json`).

## What is not handled

- **Visual:** wrist views are not re-rendered; near-camera arms re-posed by several cm can fragment.
- **Variation:** translations only (≤ 6 cm); no object rotation; no deformables (cables move rigidly near objects).
- **Physics:** no physics or contact check.
- **Evidence:** no hardware replay yet; no policy result yet.
- **Novelty:** see `NOVELTY.md` for positioning against prior work.
